answers.1: for x in a b c; do echo $x; done > /tmp/for1.txt
answers.2: for f in /tmp/logs/*.log; do wc -l < $f; done > /tmp/line_counts.txt
answers.3: for i in $(seq 1 5); do touch /tmp/seq/file$i.txt; done
answers.4: for f in /tmp/ren/*.txt; do mv "$f" "${f%.txt}.bak"; done
answers.5: for h in web1 web2 db1; do getent hosts $h; done > /tmp/hosts_check.txt
answers.6: while read name; do echo "hello $name"; done < /tmp/users.txt > /tmp/hello.txt
answers.7: for f in /tmp/chk/*.txt; do [ -s "$f" ] || rm "$f"; done
answers.8: for f in /tmp/brk/*; do n=$(basename $f); [ "$n" = stop.txt ] && break; echo $n; done > /tmp/seen.txt
